litk.a821_4yz: 4yz Transient Negative Completion reply The command was not accepted and the requested action did not occur. However, the error condition is temporary and the action may be requested again.
litk.a821_hard: It is difficult to assign a meaning to "transient" when two different sites (receiver- and sender- SMTPs) must agree on the interpretation.
litk.a821_enc: Each reply in this category might have a different time value, but the sender-SMTP is encouraged to try again.
litk.a821_thumb: A rule of thumb to determine if a reply fits into the 4yz or the 5yz category (see below) is that replies are 4yz if they can be repeated without any change in command form or in properties of the sender or receiver.
litk.a821_5yz: 5yz Permanent Negative Completion reply The command was not accepted and the requested action did not occur. The sender-SMTP is discouraged from repeating the exact request (in the same sequence).
litk.a821_human: Even some "permanent" error conditions can be corrected, so the human user may want to direct the sender-SMTP to reinitiate
litk.a1123_delay: The sender MUST delay retrying a particular destination after one attempt has failed. In general, the retry interval SHOULD be at least 30 minutes
litk.a1123_giveup: Retries continue until the message is transmitted or the sender gives up; the give-up time generally needs to be at least 4-5 days. The parameters to the retry algorithm MUST be configurable.
litk.a1123_two: policy of two connection attempts in the first hour the message is in the queue, and then backing off to once every two or three hours.
litk.a1123_queuing: Any queueing strategy MUST include: o Timeouts on all activities. See Section 5.3.2. o Never sending error messages in response to error messages.
litk.a1123_dns: retry interval SHOULD be constrained by an exponential backoff algorithm, and SHOULD also have upper and lower bounds. IMPLEMENTATION: A measured RTT and variance (if available) should be used to calculate an initial retransmission interval. If this information is not available, a default of no less than 5 seconds should be used.
litk.a1123_model: The general model of a sender-SMTP is one or more processes that periodically attempt to transmit outgoing mail.
litk.a5321_delay: The sender MUST delay retrying a particular destination after one attempt has failed. In general, the retry interval SHOULD be at least 30 minutes; however, more sophisticated and variable strategies will be beneficial when the SMTP client can determine the reason for non-delivery.
litk.a5321_giveup: Retries continue until the message is transmitted or the sender gives up; the give-up time generally needs to be at least 4-5 days. It MAY be appropriate to set a shorter maximum number of retries for non- delivery notifications and equivalent error messages than for standard messages. The parameters to the retry algorithm MUST be configurable.
litk.a5321_queuing: Any queuing strategy MUST include timeouts on all activities on a per-command basis. A queuing strategy MUST NOT send error messages in response to error messages under any circumstances.
litk.a5321_cache: 5yz responses to the MAIL command MUST NOT be cached.
litk.a5321_thumb: A rule of thumb to determine whether a reply fits into the 4yz or the 5yz category (see below) is that replies are 4yz if they can be successful if repeated without any change in command form or in properties
litk.a5321_model: The general model for an SMTP client is one or more processes that periodically attempt to transmit outgoing mail.
litk.aexim_letter: The letter identifies the algorithm for computing a new retry time; the cutoff time is the time beyond which this algorithm no longer applies
litk.aexim_meas: The cutoff time is measured from the time that the first failure for the domain (combined with the local part if relevant) was detected, not from the time the message was received.
litk.aexim_rim: retry_interval_max limits the maximum interval between retries. It cannot be set greater than 24h , which is its default value.
litk.aexim_four: the cutoff time is four days. Reaching the retry cutoff is independent of how long any specific message has been failing; it is the length of continuous failure for the recipient address that counts.
litk.aexim_30min: They happen every 30 minutes for 24 hours only.
litk.aexim_F_ds: F : retry at fixed intervals. There is a single time parameter specifying the interval.
litk.aexim_F_dj: F: retry at fixed intervals. There is a single time parameter specifying the interval.
litk.aexim_G_dj: G: retry at geometrically increasing intervals. The first argument specifies a starting value for the interval, and the second a multiplier, which is used to increase the size of the interval at each retry.
litk.aexim_H_dj: H: retry at randomized intervals. The arguments are as for G. For each retry, the previous interval is multiplied by the factor in order to get a maximum for the next interval.
